note: Named shapes the XDR schema cannot express as one union case. Detected by tools/mine.py from the decoded ledger.

signed-payload-signer.title: A signer whose key is an ed25519 signed payload (P... strkey)
signed-payload-signer.why: The key is 40 to 100 bytes, not 32. Code that assumes every signer is an account key truncates or rejects it.

signed-payload-max-length.title: Signed-payload signer with the maximum 64-byte payload
signed-payload-max-length.why: The longest legal signer key; exposes fixed-size buffers and column widths.

signed-payload-needs-padding.title: Signed-payload signer whose payload length is not a multiple of 4
signed-payload-needs-padding.why: The strkey form carries zero padding after the payload; encoders that skip or mis-size it produce a different key.

muxed-account.title: A muxed account (M... address) as source or destination
muxed-account.why: The address carries a 64-bit ID on top of the account key. Storing it in an account-key column loses the ID or corrupts the row.

muxed-id-zero.title: Muxed account with ID 0
muxed-id-zero.why: Zero is a valid ID and is distinct from a plain G... account; truthiness checks treat it as absent.

muxed-id-beyond-f64.title: Muxed account ID above 2^53
muxed-id-beyond-f64.why: Held in a floating-point number, the ID rounds to a different ID.

muxed-id-max.title: Muxed account ID 2^64-1
muxed-id-max.why: Overflows a signed 64-bit column and any float.

scaddress-muxed-account.title: A muxed account inside a contract address value (ScAddress)
scaddress-muxed-account.why: Token events can name a muxed destination; code that expects only G... and C... addresses fails or drops the ID.

scaddress-muxed-id-beyond-f64.title: Muxed ScAddress with an ID above 2^53
scaddress-muxed-id-beyond-f64.why: Same rounding hazard as a muxed account, one layer down in contract data.

scaddress-muxed-contract.title: A muxed contract address (ScAddress of the muxed-contract type)
scaddress-muxed-contract.why: New in protocol 30. Decoders on older XDR cannot read the address type at all.

soroban-created-trustline.title: A trustline created by a contract call, with no ChangeTrust operation
soroban-created-trustline.why: Indexers that derive trustline history from operation types never see it; only the ledger meta shows the new entry.

soroban-created-account.title: An account created by a contract call, with no CreateAccount operation
soroban-created-account.why: Indexers that derive account creation from operation types never see it.

scmap-keys-collide-as-text.title: A contract map whose distinct keys convert to the same text
scmap-keys-collide-as-text.why: Converting the map to a string-keyed object keeps one entry and silently drops the others.

scmap-mixed-key-types.title: A contract map with keys of more than one type
scmap-mixed-key-types.why: Key order follows the host's type order, not text order; code that re-sorts or assumes one key type misreads it.

scval-nested-5-deep.title: A contract value nested five or more levels deep
scval-nested-5-deep.why: Recursive walkers without a depth cap can be driven to exhaust the stack.

scval-int64-beyond-f64.title: A 64-bit contract integer above 2^53
scval-int64-beyond-f64.why: Loses precision in any language that holds it in a float.

scval-wide-integer.title: A 128-bit or 256-bit contract integer
scval-wide-integer.why: Needs big-integer handling; hi/lo parts are easy to combine wrongly.

auth-nested-invocations.title: A Soroban authorization entry with sub-invocations
auth-nested-invocations.why: The authorization tree is not validated for size by stellar-core beyond resource limits; walkers must handle nesting.

auth-tree-4-deep.title: A Soroban authorization tree four or more levels deep
auth-tree-4-deep.why: Unbounded recursion over the tree is one of the three mistakes the RFP's linter targets.

offer-id-beyond-f64.title: An offer ID above 2^53
offer-id-beyond-f64.why: Held in a float, it names a different offer.

pool-issuers-order-differs-strkey-vs-byt.title: A liquidity-pool asset pair whose issuers sort differently as strkey text and as key bytes
pool-issuers-order-differs-strkey-vs-byt.why: The network orders by key bytes. Code that compares G... strings rejects the valid pair or derives the wrong pool ID.

operations-at-max-100.title: A transaction with the maximum 100 operations
operations-at-max-100.why: A vector at its declared maximum; exposes off-by-one limits and per-operation cost blow-ups.

operations-50-or-more.title: A transaction with 50 or more operations
operations-50-or-more.why: Large but legal; exercises batching and operation-index arithmetic.

signatures-at-max-20.title: A transaction with the maximum 20 signatures
signatures-at-max-20.why: A vector at its declared maximum.

memo-text-not-utf8.title: A text memo whose bytes are not valid UTF-8
memo-text-not-utf8.why: stellar-core does not validate memo text. Treating it as a string corrupts it or crashes.

soroban-op-muxed-source.title: A contract invocation whose operation source is a muxed account
soroban-op-muxed-source.why: Participant extraction that renders the source as M... writes a 40-byte key where 32 are expected.

failed-transaction.title: A transaction that failed but is recorded in the ledger
failed-transaction.why: Fees are charged and the envelope is present, but its operations had no effect; envelope-derived state is wrong.

failed-soroban-transaction.title: A failed contract invocation
failed-soroban-transaction.why: The envelope claims effects that the meta shows did not happen.

tx-bad-seq-at-apply.title: A transaction in a closed ledger whose result is txBAD_SEQ
tx-bad-seq-at-apply.why: The transaction is in a closed ledger, so it passed stellar-core's checks when it was queued; it failed them when it applied, because an earlier transaction of the same ledger changed its source's state. An indexer must read validity from the result, not infer it from inclusion. Here an earlier transaction bumped the source's sequence number.

tx-bad-auth-at-apply.title: A transaction in a closed ledger whose result is txBAD_AUTH
tx-bad-auth-at-apply.why: The transaction is in a closed ledger, so it passed stellar-core's checks when it was queued; it failed them when it applied, because an earlier transaction of the same ledger changed its source's state. An indexer must read validity from the result, not infer it from inclusion. Here an earlier transaction changed the source's signers or weights, so the envelope's signatures no longer authorize it.

tx-bad-auth-extra-at-apply.title: A transaction in a closed ledger whose result is txBAD_AUTH_EXTRA
tx-bad-auth-extra-at-apply.why: The transaction is in a closed ledger, so it passed stellar-core's checks when it was queued; it failed them when it applied, because an earlier transaction of the same ledger changed its source's state. An indexer must read validity from the result, not infer it from inclusion. Here an earlier transaction raised the source's master weight, so one of the envelope's signatures went unused.

tx-bad-min-seq-age-or-gap-at-apply.title: A transaction in a closed ledger whose result is txBAD_MIN_SEQ_AGE_OR_GAP
tx-bad-min-seq-age-or-gap-at-apply.why: The transaction is in a closed ledger, so it passed stellar-core's checks when it was queued; it failed them when it applied, because an earlier transaction of the same ledger changed its source's state. An indexer must read validity from the result, not infer it from inclusion. Here an earlier transaction changed the source's sequence number in the same ledger, so a minimum sequence-ledger gap is not met.

tx-bad-sponsorship-at-apply.title: A transaction in a closed ledger whose result is txBAD_SPONSORSHIP
tx-bad-sponsorship-at-apply.why: A sponsorship sandwich left open: BeginSponsoringFutureReserves without its End. stellar-core sets the code in TransactionFrame::applyOperations, so the transaction is in the ledger, failed.

op-bad-auth-at-apply.title: An operation in a closed ledger whose result is opBAD_AUTH
op-bad-auth-at-apply.why: The operation's own source did not authorize it at apply: OperationFrame::checkSignature runs again then, and an earlier transaction of the ledger changed that source's signers. The envelope carries a signature that authorizes nothing.
